<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-summary">Summary</button></h2><div id="work-acc-summary" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">The poem narrates the story of Lord Śiva's battle against the demon Tripurāsura, who had gained immense power and had created three cities in the sky, underwater, and on earth. The demon's power had made him arrogant and he began to torment and oppress the people.<br>The gods were unable to defeat the demon and sought Lord Śiva's help. Lord Śiva agreed to help and decided to destroy the demon's cities with a single arrow. However, the arrow could only be made from the flowers of the Kurukshetra forest, which could only be obtained with the help of a devotee.<br>The gods approached the king of the Kurus, who agreed to help and sent his daughter to fetch the flowers. The king's daughter, however, fell in love with Lord Śiva and decided to help him instead. She managed to obtain the flowers and Lord Śiva was able to create the arrow.<br>In the final battle, Lord Śiva destroyed the demon's cities with the arrow and killed Tripurāsura. The poem highlights the power of devotion and the importance of seeking blessings from the divine. It also portrays Lord Śiva's compassionate nature and his willingness to forgive even his enemies.</div></div></div>

It narrates the story of Lord Śiva's battle against the demon Tripurāsura, who had gained immense power and had created three cities in the sky, underwater, and on earth.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-uniqueness">Uniqueness</button></h2><div id="work-acc-uniqueness" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">The uniqueness of &quot;Tripuradahanakāvya&quot; lies in its portrayal of Lord Śiva's compassionate nature and his willingness to forgive even his enemies. It also highlights the power of devotion and the importance of seeking blessings from the divine.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-contribution">Contribution &amp; Notes</button></h2><div id="work-acc-contribution" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">&quot;Tripuradahanakāvya&quot; is a significant contribution to Sanskrit literature. It is considered to be one of the major works of Vasudeva. The poem is known for its excellent use of language, poetic style, and intricate narrative. The poem not only reflects the author's mastery of the Sanskrit language but also his deep understanding of Indian mythology and culture.<br>The poem depicts the destruction of the three cities of the demons by Lord Śiva. It is a beautifully crafted work that tells the story of the demon trio - Tripura, who were causing havoc in the three worlds. The poem is an ode to Lord Śiva's strength, power, and invincibility. The poem's narrative structure is impressive, and it is an excellent example of how a traditional Indian epic poem should be composed.<br>Vasudeva's &quot;Tripuradahanakāvya&quot; is a valuable addition to the Sanskrit language's rich literary tradition. It is a masterpiece of poetry that showcases the author's expertise in the language and the genre. It is a significant contribution to the study of Indian mythology, culture, and religion, and it has helped to preserve these traditions for generations to come.</div></div></div>
